now.q: Is someone in the water right now?
now.help: The tree starts here every time. Nothing on this site dispatches help.

options.label: Yes
options.sub: Someone is in the water or missing on it

options.label: No
options.sub: I want to prevent the next one

emergency.title: Get help moving first.

steps.h: On the sea, a harbor or a river
steps.p: Call VHF channel 16 or the Coast Guard. In the United States, 911 also reaches them. Give a position, how many people, and the water.

steps.h: Someone on a bridge, or thinking of harm
steps.p: In the United States call or text 988. Stay with them if you safely can.
Keep your eyes on the person. Reach with anything long, throw anything that floats. Enter the water only if you are trained and equipped: untrained rescuers drown.
The first minute is the gasp. Tell the person to float and get their breathing under control before trying to swim.

emergency.note: These are the actions responders teach. They are not a substitute for a call.

water.help: A measure that works in a pool does nothing in a tide. Name the water first, then the person, then the measure.

sea-swimmers.title: Swimmers and surfers on the open coast
sea-swimmers.summary: Most coastal swimming deaths involve rips, cold water, or swimming where no one is watching. The measures with the best evidence are skills and supervision; the cold-water clock is still a question.

measures.text: Basic swimming, water-safety and safe-rescue skills for school-age children
Lifeguarded swimming areas, flags and local hazard signs: at USLA-guarded beaches the chance of drowning is about 1 in 18 million
Rip-current and float-first public messaging
A hand-size card on time in cold water (1 minute to control breathing, 10 of useful movement, about 1 hour), tested by the people it is for

count: minutes from alarm to reaching the person
sea-swimmers.adopter: A beach patrol, a town recreation department, a surf club
sea-swimmers.unknown: No one publishes a global split of drownings by water setting, so the size of this branch is unknown.

sea-small-craft.title: People in small craft offshore
sea-small-craft.summary: In the United States three in four boating deaths are drownings and 87% of those who drowned wore no life jacket. Wearing one is the strongest single measure with evidence behind it.

measures.text: Set and enforce safe boating rules
Always wear a life jacket: boaters who wore one drowned at about half the rate of those who did not (risk ratio 0.51)
Boating safety instruction: about 70% of US deaths involve an operator with none (an association, not proof)
A late-boat watch a small harbor can run this season
A one-page drift sheet whose error grows honestly

sea-small-craft.adopter: A harbormaster, a marina, a paddling club

sea-fishing.title: Fishing crews and workers
sea-fishing.summary: Somewhere between 24,000 and more than 100,000 fishers die each year, depending on who counts. Most work on boats the treaties do not reach. The first measure here is to count.

measures.text: Safe shipping and vessel rules; the Cape Town Agreement enters into force on 24 Feb 2027 for vessels of 24 m and over
One rule or one piece of kit for boats under the treaty size
Life jackets designed for working on deck
A report short enough that a tired harbor will file it

count: who reported it, and to whom
sea-fishing.adopter: A fishing co-op, a fisheries safety body, a harbormaster
sea-fishing.unknown: How much of the fishing toll is already inside WHO's 300,000 is unresolved.

sea-passengers.title: Passengers on ferries and unsafe vessels
sea-passengers.summary: Ferry deaths run to perhaps a thousand or two a year by an old estimate; deaths on migrant crossings were at least 3,650 in the year to May 2025. Neither is inside the core count.

measures.text: Set and enforce safe shipping and ferry rules, including regular inspections
Overloading enforcement and passenger counts at the dock
Search and rescue at sea for crossings: a state and NGO task; the lab keeps the count, not a pilot
A global yearly series for water-transport deaths, which does not exist

sea-passengers.adopter: A flag state, a port authority, a ferry operator
sea-passengers.unknown: No global series for water-transport deaths: the largest unmeasured piece of the toll.

harbor-working.title: Working boats and crews in the harbor
harbor-working.summary: A working harbor still learns about a late boat from a cousin. The measures here are cheap and old: a watch, a radio, a jacket, and a form.

measures.text: A late-boat watch a small harbor can run this season
A VHF radio carried, channel 16 known by every crew member
Life jackets worn on deck
A hand-size card on time in cold water
A report short enough that a tired harbor will file it

harbor-working.adopter: A harbormaster, a fishing co-op, a Coast Guard station

harbor-recreational.title: Recreational boaters and paddlers in a river mouth
harbor-recreational.summary: The Piscataqua runs near four knots at the mouth. A kayak paddles about three. The measures are a jacket, a plan, and respect for the tide table.

measures.text: Always wear a life jacket: about half the drowning risk for boaters who wear one
Boating safety instruction before the first trip
A float plan left with someone ashore; a late-boat watch to receive it
Tidal current awareness: plan around slack water
A hand-size card on time in cold water

harbor-recreational.adopter: A harbormaster, a paddling club, an outfitter

harbor-foot.title: People on foot near the water
harbor-foot.summary: Docks, seawalls, rocks and bridges. Two different problems share this branch: falls into cold water, and crisis on a bridge.

measures.text: Throw rings and reach poles at docks and seawalls, checked monthly
"Reach or throw, don't go" public messaging
For a bridge: a physical barrier. Reviews find fewer deaths at sites after barriers; the evidence is low quality and displacement is unsettled
988 signs, phones and lighting on a bridge: help, but do not restrict access

harbor-foot.adopter: A town, a harbor authority, two state DOTs
harbor-foot.unknown: There is no published annual count for the Piscataqua River Bridge. The span brief keeps what is known.

harbor-children.title: Children and teens around the harbor
harbor-children.summary: Jumping from docks and bridges, wading on a falling tide. Skills and rules, with adults who know the water.

measures.text: Basic swimming, water-safety and safe-rescue skills for school-age children
Supervised swim areas and clear rules on jumping
Life jackets for children on docks and in boats

harbor-children.adopter: A town recreation department, a sailing school, a harbormaster

lake-under5.title: Children under 5 near a lake or pond
lake-under5.summary: Nearly a quarter of the world's drowning deaths are children under five. The measures with the strongest evidence are barriers and supervised care.

measures.text: Control access to water: barriers, fencing, covered wells
Community day-care for pre-school children: village crèches in Bangladesh cut child drowning deaths by about 82%
Caregiver CPR and safe-rescue skills

lake-under5.adopter: A town, a child-care provider, a lake association

lake-children.title: Children 5–14 and teens at the lake
lake-children.summary: Drowning is a leading cause of death for children 5–14 in several regions. Skills first, then supervised places to use them.

measures.text: Basic swimming, water-safety and safe-rescue skills: SwimSafe lessons in Bangladesh cut child drowning deaths by about 93%
Lifeguarded swim areas
Ice safety education and a throw rope at known crossings

lake-children.adopter: A school district, a camp, a town

lake-adults.title: Adults at the lake
lake-adults.summary: Alcohol, cold water and no life jacket. In US boating deaths alcohol is the leading known factor.

measures.text: Always wear a life jacket on the water: about half the drowning risk
Alcohol and water don't mix: the leading known factor in US boating deaths (an association)
A hand-size card on time in cold water
Ice-rescue kit and training for the first responders who will be called

lake-adults.adopter: A lake association, a volunteer fire department

pool-under5.title: Children under 5 at a pool
pool-under5.summary: Four-sided fencing that separates the pool from the house is the measure with the clearest evidence.

measures.text: Four-sided fencing that separates the pool from the house, with a self-latching gate: a quarter of the odds of drowning versus no fence
Supervision within arm's reach, with one adult named as the watcher
Caregiver CPR

pool-under5.adopter: A town building department, a homeowners' association, a pool company

pool-children.title: Children and teens at a pool

measures.text: Swimming and water-safety lessons
Lifeguards and posted rules at public pools

pool-children.adopter: A school, a town pool, a swim club

pool-adults.title: Adults at a pool
pool-adults.summary: Alcohol, swimming alone and medical conditions.

measures.text: Never swim alone
Alcohol away from the water
Lifeguards at public pools

home-under5.title: Children under 5 at home
home-under5.summary: Baths, buckets, wells and tanks. In low-income settings this is where a large share of under-five drownings happen. The WHO investment case puts day-care and swim skills at the center.

measures.text: Cover wells and tanks; empty buckets and baths after use; doorway barriers and playpens
Community day-care for pre-school children: crèches cut child drowning deaths by about 82% in Bangladesh
Caregiver safe-rescue skills

home-under5.adopter: A health ministry, an NGO running day-care, a village council

flood-before.title: A community before the flood
flood-before.summary: Three in four flood-disaster deaths are drownings. Preparedness and early warning are the measures WHO recommends.

measures.text: Flood preparedness, planning and early warning
Marked evacuation routes to high ground, practiced
Count flood drownings as drownings so they appear in the ledger

flood-before.adopter: A municipality, a national disaster agency
flood-before.unknown: Flood drownings sit outside the core count. We estimate 3,000–8,000 a year and call that a band, not a count.

flood-during.title: A household in a flood
flood-during.summary: Moving water takes cars and people. The measure is not to enter it.

measures.text: Do not walk or drive through moving water
Move to high ground early, before routes close
Call the local emergency number for anyone in the water

count: entered water on foot or in a vehicle
flood-during.adopter: A household; the lab has no pilot here
